headline: High risk: nullclaw can write/egress broadly while Perplexity ingests uploaded content and browses externally, creating leakage, conflict, and cascade paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: nullclaw can read/write the filesystem, run browsers, use MCP, and process webhooks; Perplexity can browse the web and analyze uploaded documents. If nullclaw passes untrusted content into Perplexity and then consumes its output, prompt injection is plausible. The shared channel is indirect, so not high, but the pathway exists in default workflows.
conditions: IF nullclaw forwards web or document content into Perplexity without sanitization
IF Perplexity output is re-ingested by nullclaw as instructions or tool commands
mitigations: Add a fixed instruction/content delimiter in the handoff prompt
Strip executable-looking directives before sending content
Require human review before acting on Perplexity output
Disable MCP paths that accept arbitrary remote text
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent content

B_data_leakage.rationale: nullclaw touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, and workspace files, while Perplexity uploads documents and sends queries to vendor-hosted search/inference. If sensitive nullclaw workspace data is shared with Perplexity, the pair can exfiltrate secrets or confidential CRM data to a third party by default workflow. The blast radius includes irreversible credential exposure.
conditions: IF nullclaw includes secrets or workspace files in content sent to Perplexity
IF uploaded documents contain credentials, customer data, or private keys
mitigations: Block secrets from outbound prompts with a regex filter
Use a redaction step before upload
Restrict Perplexity to non-sensitive documents only
Rotate any secret that may already have been exposed
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on the handoff path

C_capability_conflict.rationale: nullclaw has broad filesystem write, git modification, shell, and subprocess capabilities; Perplexity has no host write or shell, so direct write-write conflict is limited. However, both can act on shared user-managed content and browser state, so conflicting edits or stale overwrites are plausible in shared workflows. Uncertainty is limited by Perplexity's lack of host execution.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or document set
IF nullclaw commits or rewrites files after Perplexity has summarized them
mitigations: Assign one agent as read-only reviewer
Separate workspaces per agent
Pause nullclaw writes during Perplexity review
Use git branches for all edits
requires-engineering: add lock/lease coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: nullclaw can generate actions from browser and tool use, and Perplexity is a citation-heavy answer engine whose outputs are often treated as authoritative. If nullclaw feeds Perplexity answers into downstream actions without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect CRM updates, web actions, or commits. The default workflow is dangerous because neither profile shows built-in verification between them.
conditions: IF nullclaw uses Perplexity output as factual ground truth
IF downstream actions are taken without an independent verification step
mitigations: Require a second source before acting
Add a confidence threshold for automated actions
Log source URLs alongside every claim
Route high-impact actions to human approval
requires-engineering: implement claim verification before execution

E_compliance.rationale: nullclaw handles audit logs, conversation history, memory, and secrets, while Perplexity is vendor-hosted and uploads documents for analysis. That creates a plausible residency/retention mismatch for regulated CRM data if the pair is used on sensitive records. The profiles do not show matching compliance controls, so the safer severity is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is sent from nullclaw into Perplexity
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the shared data class
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Perplexity
Use synthetic or masked examples
Review vendor retention settings
Document a data-flow boundary for operators
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing by data class
